aboutMore: the part i dont put in albums: my nana gave me her Pentax last winter and thats the real reason i started. it came with a roll of film still inside, 24 exposures, never developed. i didnt tell anyone about that until the blog. i also babysit the Abernathy twins (5) on tuesdays and thursdays, who are my favorite models because they never ask to see the screen. i develop my own black and white in the school darkroom, room 9, red light, smells like a swimming pool made of vinegar. the dutch angle is a style. every horizon in my nanas pictures is perfectly level. i am working through that.

blog.title: what was on the roll in nanas pentax
blog.body: ms pham let me stay after school in the darkroom. i developed it myself. developer, 6 min, stop bath, fixer. theres a point where the paper just starts to show up in the tray and u stand there like ur watching a ghost get its face on. 24 frames. 22 are the kitchen window. the same one. light coming in over a bowl of lemons, over and over, like she was trying to get it right. frame 23 is a thumb. frame 24 is me, about 8, in a yellow rain slicker, holding a jar with 2 tadpoles in it, and i am the only crooked thing in the whole roll, bc i was leaning. every horizon on that roll is dead level. she never tilted once. i stood there in the red light for like 20 minutes. i dont know if that is a joke or a confession. im calling it a style. the lemons are on my desktop now. i havent told her yet. i think im going to bring her the print and not say anything. she'll know.

blog.title: the abernathy twins photo shoot (tuesday) (behind the scenes)
blog.body: wren and otto are 5. i shoot them for 90 minutes before bath time and they are the only clients i have ever had who dont check the back of the camera. cast: wren (only photographed from the left, thats her good side, shes been clear), otto (is a 'dinosaur lawyer' and wears a tie made of tin foil and objects loudly). props: one cardboard box, a wizard hat, my fisheye. otto said the fisheye pics looked like 'a fish took them.' i have never been so hurt or so inspired. wren asked if she was 'pretty or just in focus' and i said 'in focus is better' and she nodded like i had said something wise. i deleted the one where otto licked the lens. i kept the one after, where he looks like he is sorry and also not sorry. their mom asked for a print of the box one, the one where they both look in different directions, and PAID me $15. real money. a lady in a cardigan paid me for a photograph. i bought a chai and sat on the curb and looked at the money.

blog.title: yearbook is not my friend: a shot list (with notes from yvette in red)
blog.body: yvette asked me to shoot the powderpuff game for the yearbook. rules, as stated: 1. horizon LEVEL 2. faces centered 3. names left to right in the caption 4. no one mid-sneeze. policy: 3 tilts per spread, 'intentional and tasteful.' i said i would try. i got 211 frames. 80 were level. 11 had a sneeze. the rest were tilted, bc powderpuff is basically a parade of people falling down and the best way to see that is on a diagonal. the contact sheet came back w/ 'TILT' in red pen next to 14 frames, and next to 9 others she just wrote 'hm.' hm is worse. i reshot the second half level, like a hostage. my wrist hurt. one tilted pic made it into the spread. page 31, bottom right, the corner of the gym. i used 1 of my 3. i'm saving the other 2 like a squirrel. the caption, which i also wrote, says 'left to right: kim, whitney, someone mid-sneeze.' (i didnt get her name)

blog.title: disposable cameras, ranked (a buyers guide nobody asked for)
blog.body: i have shot 61 disposables since june. i have opinions. 1. the Fuji QuickSnap, 27 exp: best colors, flash is bright and angry, perfect for people mid-yell. 2. the Kodak FunSaver, 27 exp: friendly, a little yellow, it makes everyone look like they are at a barbecue in a photo your uncle took. 3. the drugstore store-brand: i dont know what it is, the pictures come back as just light. i keep a few for emergencies and for pics of ppl who dont want to be found. 4. the waterproof one: i took it in the bathtub, the pictures are of my knees. 5. the black and white one: unbeatable. u cant take a bad picture. u can only take a sad one. NOTES: the flash takes 8 seconds to recharge and everyone assumes the picture is over and walks away. do not tell them. take the second one. that's where the real face is.

survey.title: photographers survey (copied from a lomography forum, answered at 1 am)
qa: camera you shoot with most:
the holga. the canon powershot gets used more but the holga gets LOVED more. thats the difference
favorite film:
fuji 400. cheap, forgiving, makes the sky look like the inside of a seashell
worst photo you ever took that you kept:
my own thumb, frame 23, nanas pentax. its not worse than the others. its just a thumb. i love it
something you regret not shooting:
my nana at the kitchen window w/ a lemon in her hand. i saw it. i didnt have the camera. i have the memory, which is the same thing but fewer prints
how many undeveloped rolls do you own:
9. i know. i know. i'm scared of what's on them
best light:
4pm in november, on a wet street, 20 minutes before it gets dark. the light does a thing
person who has never let you photograph them:
my dad. but he's in the background of everything. he's the horizon
do you tilt:
yes. it's on purpose. i can level a horizon. i just dont want to
favorite place to shoot:
the parking garage on 4th at golden hour. its the only place in portland where the light and the concrete agree
a rule you break:
dont shoot into the sun. i shoot into the sun. i like when the lens gets mad
what would you photograph if you could photograph anything:
the second right before someone starts laughing. the whole face is deciding
last thing you took a picture of:
a pigeon on a bus shelter eating a french fry the size of its head. it was perfect. it was level. i know. i know

dms: ms pham gave me a key to the darkroom. an actual key. i have been a person with a key for 3 hours and i have never felt so powerful. i went in and turned the red light on just to look at it. i didnt even develop anything. i just stood there in the red
otto asked me today what a photograph is. i said its a thing that remembers for you. he said 'so its like a mom.' i have to go lie down on the carpet and think about that for a while
it has rained 9 days in a row. the lens fogs, the film curls, my nana says only tourists use umbrellas. i own 4 umbrellas. i am a tourist in my own city

i got my first fan. a woman at the chai cart saw my album on the screen of my camera and said she liked the one of her cup. she is 61 and sells tea. she is my first fan. she gave me a free chai. i cried a little into the chai

im shooting the same tree every day for 30 days. day 17 a squirrel was in it. day 23 there was a man in a banana suit under it. day 30 is tomorrow. i am afraid the tree will be the star

random question i always wonder. when u look at a picture, do u look at the person first or the corner? i look at the corner. ive done it since i was little. i think thats why my horizons are the way they are

yvette asked me to shoot the whole senior class on the bleachers for the panorama. 340 people. i tilted it 2 degrees. now 340 people are leaning left. she has not said anything yet. she has not said anything in 2 days. i am afraid of her silence
